title: Regional GPU provisioning playout - experiment sheet (Sep 2026)
summary: Working spreadsheet capturing a set of controlled playouts for autoscaler parameter combinations across 4 regions. Goal: find configs that keep p95 latency <= 150ms for hosted API steady-state traffic while minimizing average idle GPUs and spike cost. This is a working doc with raw observations and proposed defaults for canary rollout.
assumptions: 1) Each GPU pod = 1x A100-80GB equivalent; 2) Typical inference concurrency per GPU = 120 tokens/s (baseline model mix); 3) Traffic patterns simulated with prerecorded traces (weekdays peak + randomized spikes); 4) Regional capacity constraints: us-west1 and eu-west1 primary, ap-southeast1 burst only; 5) Cold start penalty ~220ms when scaling from 0->1.

observations:
- Hysteresis matters: moving from 30s->300s hysteresis reduced flapping but increased idle by ~8-12% across runs.
- MinGPUs tradeoff: min>=3 avoided most cold-start p95 spikes in primary regions.
- Scale step size: larger step reduces number of scaling ops but can temporarily overprovision; smaller step yields smoother latency but more API churn.
- Regions behave differently: ap-southeast1 suffers from longer provisioning times (measured +80ms extra cold start) due to limited local capacity in the test cloud provider.
- Cost vs latency: aggressive scale-up (low trigger threshold + large steps) lowered p95 by ~10-20% in peak windows but increased short-term cost by ~15-20% in playouts with repeated spikes.
- Observed anomalies: one run (AggressiveUp) had sustained >400ms p95 for 6 minutes because autoscaler trimmed pods after transient success; root cause likely feedback loop between router health-checks and autoscaler metrics.
- Unresolved: whether to bias autoscaler metrics to tail-latency signal vs. CPU/GPU utilization for mixed-model workloads.
cost_estimates:
Estimated incremental cost changes vs baseline-1 for a 30 day projected workload (mixed):
- ConservativeMin: +12.4% ($+32k/month for primary cluster)
- AggressiveUp: +18.7% ($+49k/month) but ~12% lower error-budget consumption for latency SLAs
- HysteresisLong: +4.9% ($+13k/month) with much lower ops churn
- AdaptiveMix: +3.7% ($+9.7k/month) recommended tradeoff
Notes: numbers include GPU runtime and ephemeral bootstrap cost; networking and storage not included.
recommended_policy:
Proposed default for hosted-api primary regions (canary + 2-week burn):
- MinGPUs: 3 for us-west1/eu-west1, 0 for ap-southeast1 but with warm pool of 1 prewarmed pod when predicted spike probability > 35%
- MaxGPUs: region-specific (us-west1 64, eu-west1 48, ap-southeast1 20, ca-central1 48)
- ScaleUpTrigger: 62% utilization (or observed p95 > 150ms averaged across 30s)
- ScaleDownTrigger: 28% utilization with 180s hysteresis
- ScaleStep: 2x for scale-up when spike detected (capped at +10 GPUs per event), step=1 for scale-down
- Observability: track p95, GPU-util, idle_gpus, and scale_ops per minute; alert if >3 scale events in 10m or sustained p95 >200ms for 5m
Rationale: keeps latency SLOs in primary regions while limiting steady-state idle and ops churn.
